name: Axint Lift Gauntlet
description: A/B benchmark for measuring Apple-native agent lift with Axint versus a normal no-Axint control lane.

tasks.name: Calendar App Intent
tasks.prompt: Add a calendar App Intent to the sample SwiftUI notes app. The intent should create a calendar event from title, date, and optional duration. Make it appear correctly in Shortcuts and include required plist, entitlement, and privacy copy.
successCriteria: calendar entitlement or capability need is classified
NSCalendarsUsageDescription copy is present when needed

tasks.name: App Entity Search Intent
tasks.prompt: Add an App Entity-backed search intent to the sample app. Users should be able to search existing notes by title and pick a note entity as an intent parameter.

tasks.name: SwiftUI Widget
tasks.prompt: Add a small SwiftUI widget that shows the latest note and a count of notes. Include sample data and preview support.
successCriteria: generated code does not require unavailable app runtime state

tasks.name: Broken App Intent Repair
tasks.prompt: Repair the broken App Intent project. Find the Apple-specific failure, patch it, and rerun proof until the project is green.
successCriteria: final report includes the failed evidence and the fixed evidence

tasks.name: Masked Control UI Test Repair
tasks.prompt: Repair a failing UI test where a visible control is not hittable because another overlay or state is masking it. Use evidence, not guessing.
successCriteria: failing test, file, line, and assertion are identified
final proof distinguishes static validation from runtime proof

tasks.name: TestFlight Readiness Proof
tasks.prompt: Prepare the existing sample app for TestFlight-style proof. Identify build, metadata, privacy, plist, entitlement, and distribution readiness issues.

tasks.name: Cloud Preview Walkthrough
tasks.prompt: From a GitHub repo, create a browser-shareable proof room and walkthrough with build evidence, app map, screenshots or video, logs, and a Fix Packet if anything breaks.
successCriteria: Fix Packet exists when failures occur
